title: Dukes of Hazzard Plymouth Fury Cop Car Appears on Bring a Trailer
summary: This 1971 Plymouth Sport Fury police car in full Hazzard County regalia is ready for Roscoe P. Coltrane.
whatHappening: A 1971 Plymouth Sport Fury police car decked out in full Dukes of Hazzard regalia—complete with Hazzard County markings—is currently listed for sale on Bring a Trailer. The vehicle is styled to match the iconic patrol car driven by Sheriff Rosco P. Coltrane in the classic television series.
whoInvolved: Car and Driver reports on the listing, which features a piece of television history from the hit CBS series The Dukes of Hazzard. The show aired from 1979 to 1985 and became a cultural phenomenon, ranking among the most-watched programs of its era.
whyMatters: The sale highlights enduring collector interest in vehicles tied to beloved television properties from the 1970s and 1980s. Authentic or replica police cars from major TV shows command premium prices and attract enthusiasts who value both the automotive craftsmanship and nostalgia factor. This listing demonstrates how pop culture memorabilia continues to drive value in the classic car market.
articleBody:
A 1971 Plymouth Sport Fury wearing the unmistakable livery of Hazzard County's finest is headed to auction on Bring a Trailer, offering collectors a chance to own a tangible piece of television history. The car, finished in full Dukes of Hazzard police regalia, captures the aesthetic of the patrol vehicle famously driven by Sheriff Rosco P. Coltrane throughout the series' run.

The Dukes of Hazzard aired on CBS from 1979 to 1985 for seven seasons and 147 episodes, becoming a fixture of American popular culture during the late 1970s and early 1980s. At its peak, the show ranked among the top-viewed television series in the nation, at one point trailing only Dallas in viewership. The series' blend of action, comedy, and rural charm resonated with audiences across the country, and its iconic vehicles—including the General Lee and Rosco's patrol car—became instantly recognizable symbols of the show.

The 1971 Plymouth Sport Fury represents a significant moment in the marque's history. The Plymouth Fury, produced from 1955 until 1989, was introduced as a sub-series of the Plymouth Belvedere before becoming a separate model line one level above the Belvedere starting in 1959. By 1971, the Fury was positioned as a full-size car—a class it maintained from 1965 through 1974—making it an ideal choice for law enforcement and television production purposes. The Sport Fury variant offered additional styling and performance options, lending it the aggressive stance required for a television sheriff's vehicle.

According to Car and Driver, the car's authenticity and condition will likely determine its final sale price. Vehicles with genuine connections to major television properties have proven attractive to a dedicated collector base willing to pay premiums for documented provenance. Whether this particular example is an original used in the series or a period-correct recreation, it represents the intersection of automotive history and television nostalgia that continues to drive interest in the collector market.

The listing serves as a reminder of how television properties from the network era have created lasting demand for associated memorabilia. As streaming services and modern programming dominate the cultural landscape, the tangible artifacts of classic television—especially those as substantial as a full-size automobile—have become increasingly valuable to enthusiasts seeking to preserve that legacy. For serious collectors of television history or Plymouth enthusiasts, this 1971 Sport Fury offers a rare opportunity to own a vehicle forever linked to one of CBS's greatest hits.

The company has long been regarded as a British cultural icon, particularly following its association with James Bond films and its reputation for expensive grand touring cars since the 1950s.
whyMatters: The DB12 S Volante represents an evolution of Aston Martin's grand touring portfolio, expanding convertible options for luxury car buyers seeking open-air driving experiences. This model release demonstrates Aston Martin's continued commitment to offering variants of its modern lineup, following the DB12's introduction as the DB11 replacement in May 2023.
articleBody:

The images provide potential buyers and enthusiasts with a comprehensive visual preview of how the soft-top variant compares to its hardtop counterpart, showcasing details that define the model's appearance.

The DB12 S Volante arrives as part of Aston Martin's broader strategy to refresh its grand touring portfolio. By extending the DB12 nameplate to include a convertible variant, Aston Martin aims to capture buyers who prioritize open-air driving in a luxury grand touring package.

Aston Martin has maintained its position as a manufacturer of prestigious sports cars and grand tourers since its founding in 1913. The brand gained widespread cultural recognition through its association with the James Bond franchise, most notably the DB5 featured in the 1964 film Goldfinger, an association that has endured and contributed to the marque's status as a British cultural icon. The release of exterior photography according to Car and Driver marks a typical step in the automotive product reveal cycle, allowing consumers to develop familiarity with a vehicle's styling before official launch events or availability announcements. With the 2027 model year designation, the DB12 S Volante represents Aston Martin's continued evolution of its modern grand touring lineup. The model capitalizes on the DB12's foundation while offering the traditional appeal of convertible driving that remains a cornerstone of luxury automobile desirability. The combination of Aston Martin's heritage, brand positioning, and modern grand touring capability positions this variant as a significant entry in the premium open-air sports car segment.

title: Fiat's Tiny Topolino Is Proving to Be a Popular Golf-Cart Substitute
summary: With limited street use, this little 8-hp electric runabout is attracting a lot of attention from affluent communities.
whatHappening: Fiat's new Topolino, a tiny 8-horsepower electric vehicle, is gaining traction as an alternative to golf carts in wealthy residential communities. The pint-sized runabout is drawing considerable interest despite restrictions on where it can be driven.
whoInvolved: Fiat Automobiles S.p.A., the Italian automaker tracing its roots back to 1899, is behind the Topolino's development and launch. The vehicle is attracting affluent communities as a practical, stylish alternative to traditional golf carts for limited local transportation.
whyMatters: The Topolino's popularity signals a shift in how wealthy neighborhoods approach short-distance mobility, moving beyond the utilitarian golf cart model toward design-conscious electric vehicles. This trend could reshape the micro-mobility market and influence how other automakers approach ultra-compact urban transport, especially as electric vehicle adoption accelerates in niche markets.
articleBody:
Fiat's latest addition to its lineup is proving to be an unexpected hit in an unlikely market segment. The Topolino, a diminutive electric runabout with just 8 horsepower, is gaining favor among residents of affluent communities as a quirky and practical substitute for the traditional golf cart. With its compact dimensions and modest power output, the vehicle occupies a peculiar niche—too small and underpowered for conventional road use in most jurisdictions, yet increasingly appealing to those seeking an alternative to gas-powered golf carts.

The Topolino represents a notable departure from Fiat's traditional product strategy. The Italian automaker, which has manufactured vehicles since the company's founding in 1899 with the FIAT 3½ HP, built its reputation on practical, affordable vehicles. While Fiat's iconic 500 model—produced from 1957 to 1975 as an economy city car—captured hearts across Europe and beyond, the Topolino takes the brand's philosophy of compact, clever design to an entirely new extreme. According to Car and Driver, this little electric runabout is attracting considerable attention from affluent communities seeking both functionality and distinctive character in their local transportation options.

The appeal of the Topolino lies in its intersection of Italian design pedigree and practical utility. Where a standard golf cart offers basic transportation with minimal aesthetic consideration, the Topolino brings styling, brand heritage, and the novelty of electric power to a market accustomed to utilitarian vehicles. For residents of gated communities and resort areas where street use is limited, the vehicle's modest 8-horsepower electric motor and compact frame become features rather than limitations.

This development underscores a broader shift in how affluent communities approach short-distance mobility. Rather than accepting off-the-shelf golf carts as the default choice, residents increasingly seek vehicles that reflect their values and aesthetic preferences. The Topolino's emergence in this segment suggests that automakers have identified an opportunity to serve niche markets with purpose-built electric vehicles that combine practicality with design sophistication.

The success of the Topolino in this niche may also influence how Fiat and other manufacturers think about ultra-compact vehicles in general. With restrictions on street use limiting its broader market potential, the vehicle serves primarily affluent communities where cost is less a barrier than desire for novelty and quality. This positioning allows Fiat to explore electric mobility in a segment where traditional automakers have largely ceded ground to golf cart manufacturers, potentially opening new possibilities for how small-scale electric vehicles are designed and marketed.

title: BMW and Kith Team Up to Build a One-Off X5 with a V-10 and a Manual
summary: The first X5 correctly predicted the popularity of crossovers, and this one is as appealing as they get.
whatHappening: BMW has partnered with fashion and lifestyle brand Kith to create a unique one-off X5 that combines a V-10 engine with a manual transmission—a rare combination in modern SUVs. This bespoke build represents an unusual meeting of automotive performance and luxury lifestyle branding.
whoInvolved: BMW is the German luxury automaker that pioneered the crossover segment with the original X5 in 1999. Kith is a New York-based fashion and lifestyle brand known for high-end collaborations across multiple industries, including automotive partnerships.
whyMatters: The project highlights growing demand among collectors and enthusiasts for distinctive, manually-shifted luxury vehicles at a time when such drivetrains are nearly extinct in production cars. It also demonstrates how legacy automakers are exploring creative partnerships to maintain brand relevance and appeal to niche markets beyond traditional marketing channels.
articleBody:
BMW and the lifestyle brand Kith have joined forces to create a one-of-a-kind X5 that reimagines what a luxury crossover can be, equipping it with a V-10 engine paired to a manual transmission—a powertrain combination that feels increasingly rare in today's automotive landscape. The build celebrates the appeal of driver engagement in a segment long defined by convenience and automatic gearboxes.

The X5, which made its debut in 1999 as the E53 model, represented BMW's first serious entry into the booming SUV market and proved prescient in predicting the segment's eventual dominance in global sales. Early iterations of the X5 were available with either a manual or automatic gearbox, though that flexibility disappeared as the model evolved. The second-generation E70, launched in 2006, featured only an automatic transmission paired with BMW's xDrive all-wheel-drive system, a direction the brand has maintained ever since.

This collaboration with Kith arrives at a moment when manual transmissions have become luxury items themselves. The V-10 engine—likely sourced from BMW's performance division—pairs raw mechanical power with the direct mechanical connection that a three-pedal setup provides. According to Car and Driver, the resulting one-off is as appealing as the X5 segment gets, bridging the gap between everyday practicality and driver-focused performance in ways that factory options rarely attempt.

The partnership reflects a broader shift in how premium brands engage with niche audiences. Rather than rely solely on traditional advertising, BMW and Kith are creating a conversation piece—a vehicle that appeals to both automotive enthusiasts and the lifestyle brand's fashion-forward clientele. The exclusivity of a single build, combined with the mechanical authenticity of a manual gearbox and high-performance engine, taps into a collector's mentality that values rarity and substance over mass-market convenience.

While the one-off nature of this project means it will remain a curiosity rather than a market indicator, it underscores enduring appetite among certain buyers for vehicles that prioritize engagement and mechanical honesty. The X5's evolution from a first-generation model available with manual gears to a segment dominated by slick automatics illustrates how far the industry has drifted from driver-centric design—making this Kith collaboration a potent reminder of what premium driving can still feel like.

title: 1988 Mazda 323 GTX on Bring a Trailer
summary: You’ve heard of the Evo and the WRX, but have you ever heard of Mazda’s rally-inspired 323 GTX?
whatHappening: A 1988 Mazda 323 GTX is currently listed for auction on Bring a Trailer, bringing renewed attention to Mazda's overlooked rally-inspired compact car from the late 1980s.
whoInvolved: Bring a Trailer, an automotive auction platform acquired by Hearst in 2020, is hosting the sale. Mazda, the Japanese automaker that produced the 323 GTX as part of its Familia line, engineered the rally-focused variant.
whyMatters: The 323 GTX represents a forgotten chapter in Mazda's performance history that often gets overshadowed by more famous rally machines. The listing highlights a growing collector interest in obscure Japanese performance cars and underscores how many significant automotive achievements remain unknown to mainstream enthusiasts.
articleBody:
Mazda's 323 GTX is emerging from relative obscurity as a 1988 example hits the auction block on Bring a Trailer. The car represents a chapter in Mazda's performance heritage that few enthusiasts outside rally circles ever knew existed—a genuine rally-inspired variant that predated the brand's later, more celebrated performance efforts.

The Mazda 323, part of the Familia line manufactured by Mazda between 1963 and 2003, was a small family car that prioritized practicality for most of its production run. However, the GTX variant tapped into Mazda's rallying DNA, offering buyers a compact, turbocharged package with genuine performance credentials. The model occupied a unique niche in the late-1980s Japanese automotive landscape, arriving during an era when rally heritage mattered to manufacturers looking to prove their engineering prowess.

According to Car and Driver, the 323 GTX often gets overshadowed by more famous rally icons like the Mitsubishi Evolution and Subaru WRX, both of which launched in the 1990s and achieved far greater mainstream recognition. Yet Mazda's offering demonstrates that the company was already exploring performance variants of its core lineup before those rivals emerged. The GTX's presence on Bring a Trailer signals that collectors are beginning to recognize these overlooked machines as worthy additions to performance car collections.

The listing itself highlights a broader shift in the classic and collector car market. Bring a Trailer has become a destination for discovering cars that might otherwise languish in private collections or be lost to time. By bringing the 323 GTX to auction, the platform exposes enthusiasts to vehicles that challenge conventional narratives about which manufacturers and models matter in automotive history.

The Familia line itself endured for four decades, finally being replaced by the Mazda3 and Axela in 2004. The 323 GTX represents a particular moment when Mazda combined practical small-car engineering with turbocharged performance ambitions. As interest in Japanese performance cars continues to grow among collectors, previously forgotten models like the 323 GTX are finding new audiences willing to recognize their significance.

title: 2026 Aston Martin DB12 S Volante Drive: Can a $300K Convertible Be the Rational Choice?
summary: Allow us to make the case.
whatHappening: Car and Driver has published a first drive review of the 2026 Aston Martin DB12 S Volante, a $300,000 convertible grand tourer, making the case that such an expensive open-air sports car can be a defensible purchase choice.
whoInvolved: Aston Martin, the British luxury automaker founded in 1913, is behind the DB12 S Volante—the convertible variant of the DB12 grand tourer that debuted in 2023 as the successor to the DB11. Car and Driver, a prominent automotive publication, conducted the first drive evaluation.
whyMatters: The review addresses a tension in the luxury car market: whether a vehicle at the $300,000 price point can justify its cost as anything other than a status symbol. For enthusiasts and affluent buyers, the answer could reshape how they evaluate convertible grand tourers against competitors and alternative investments.
articleBody:
Aston Martin's decision to offer the DB12 as a Volante convertible opens up a compelling proposition in the high-end automotive market. The 2026 model, priced at approximately $300,000, asks a straightforward question: can a convertible grand tourer at this price point be genuinely rational? According to Car and Driver, the answer may be yes, and they've set out to make the case in a comprehensive first drive.

The DB12 S Volante inherits its lineage from one of automotive history's most storied nameplates. Aston Martin, long regarded as a British cultural icon and producer of expensive grand touring cars since the 1950s and 1960s, cemented its reputation for luxury and performance through models like the legendary DB5—famously featured in the 1964 James Bond film Goldfinger. The DB12, which replaced the DB11 when it arrived in May 2023, continues that grand touring tradition with a modern sensibility and the added versatility of a retractable convertible roof.

The argument for rationality in a $300,000 convertible rests on several pillars: engineering quality, driving dynamics, exclusivity, and the experiential value of open-air motoring at the highest levels of performance. Grand tourers occupy a unique niche—they are designed to cover long distances in comfort and style while maintaining genuine performance credentials. A convertible variant amplifies that experiential dimension, allowing drivers to fully engage with their surroundings while benefiting from the sophisticated mechanical package beneath the skin.

For buyers in this segment, the consideration is rarely about transportation efficiency or value-per-mile. Instead, the decision hinges on whether the particular car delivers the intangible qualities that justify its premium: Does it feel special? Does it perform at a level that honors its price? Does it offer something distinct from competitors? The DB12 S Volante's Aston Martin pedigree—backed by a century of luxury sports car manufacturing—positions it as a credible contender in a rarefied market.

The convertible variant also represents a calculated risk on Aston Martin's part. Open-air grand tourers at this price point appeal to a smaller audience than their hardtop counterparts, yet they command a meaningful premium. For those who prioritize the sensory experience of driving and the distinctive character that comes with a convertible platform, the DB12 S Volante offers a compelling alternative to closed-top competitors, potentially tilting the equation in favor of rationality.

title: NHTSA Opens Investigation into GM V-8s That Won’t Stop Imploding
summary: Despite General Motors issuing a remedy for its L87 6.2-liter V-8s, NHTSA has received reports that hundreds have failed after the fix.
whatHappening: The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration has launched an investigation into General Motors' L87 6.2-liter V-8 engines after hundreds reportedly failed even after GM issued a factory remedy. The ongoing engine failures suggest the company's fix may not be addressing the root cause of the problem.
whoInvolved: General Motors Company, an American multinational automotive manufacturer headquartered in Detroit and the largest automaker in the United States by total sales, is at the center of the issue. The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration, a federal agency under the Department of Transportation responsible for automobile safety regulations, is now investigating the matter.
whyMatters: Engine failures that persist after a manufacturer's remedy raises serious safety concerns for vehicle owners and questions the effectiveness of GM's repair solution. A widespread defect in a high-performance engine used across multiple GM brands could result in costly recalls, loss of consumer confidence, and potential legal liability for the company.
articleBody:
The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration is moving forward with an investigation into General Motors' troubled L87 6.2-liter V-8 engines, marking an escalation in a problem that has plagued the automaker despite its earlier intervention. According to Car and Driver, NHTSA has received reports documenting hundreds of engine failures that occurred after General Motors issued a remedy designed to fix the underlying defect. The persistence of these failures after an attempted fix suggests the problem may be more complex or widespread than initially addressed.

General Motors, the largest automaker in the United States by total sales, manufactures the L87 V-8 across several of its automobile divisions, including Chevrolet, Buick, GMC, and Cadillac. The engine's use across multiple premium and performance vehicle lines means that any systemic defect could affect a substantial portion of the company's current customer base. The company's decision to issue a remedy earlier indicated it had identified what it believed to be the cause, but the subsequent failures suggest that diagnosis may have been incomplete.

The NHTSA investigation will likely focus on determining why the remedy failed to resolve the issue for hundreds of owners. Federal safety regulators have the authority to compel manufacturers to conduct broader recalls if evidence suggests a defect poses a safety risk. The scope of the current problem remains unclear, but the volume of post-repair failures documented by NHTSA indicates this is not an isolated incident affecting a small number of vehicles.

For General Motors, the investigation represents a significant challenge to its reputation for quality, particularly given its position as the nation's largest automaker. A failed remedy can be more damaging than an initial defect, as it raises questions about the company's engineering capabilities and the thoroughness of its quality control processes. Owners who had their vehicles serviced under the remedy may face extended downtime if NHTSA determines a more comprehensive repair is necessary.

The investigation's outcome could result in an expanded recall affecting thousands of vehicles. General Motors will be required to cooperate fully with NHTSA's inquiry and may face penalties if the agency determines the company knew about the defect's persistence and failed to act appropriately. The case underscores the regulatory scrutiny that major automakers face when safety-related defects emerge.

title: 2027 Genesis G70 Ditches V-6 for What Could Be Its Final Year on Sale
summary: Documents show that the turbo four will be the only choice going forward, with the twin-turbo 3.3-liter sadly leaving the lineup.
whatHappening: Genesis has confirmed that the 2027 G70 will drop its twin-turbo 3.3-liter V-6 engine, leaving only a turbo four-cylinder as the powertrain option. The move signals what could be the final generation for this compact luxury sedan before potential discontinuation.
whoInvolved: Genesis is the luxury vehicle brand of South Korea's Hyundai Motor Group, established as an independent marque in 2015. The brand, known for its "Athletic Elegance" design philosophy, produces vehicles at facilities in Ulsan and designs them across locations including Rüsselsheim, Namyang, and Irvine.
whyMatters: The elimination of the V-6 reflects Genesis's shift toward smaller, more efficient engines amid tightening emissions regulations and changing consumer preferences. If the 2027 model year is indeed the G70's last, it would mark the end of a model that has been central to Genesis's entry-level luxury portfolio since the brand's inception.
articleBody:
The 2027 Genesis G70 is losing one of its defining features. According to Car and Driver, internal documents reveal that the compact luxury sedan will be powered exclusively by a turbocharged four-cylinder engine, effectively ending the reign of the twin-turbo 3.3-liter V-6 that has been available in the model since its introduction.

The move represents a significant downsizing for a vehicle class traditionally defined by multi-cylinder prestige. The twin-turbo 3.3 has long served as a signature powerplant for Genesis, offering performance credentials befitting the brand's luxury positioning. Its discontinuation suggests the automaker is consolidating its engine portfolio—a common industry response to increasingly stringent fuel economy and emissions standards.

Genesis, the luxury arm of South Korea's Hyundai Motor Group, has built its reputation around design and engineering excellence since its establishment as an independent brand in 2015. The G70, positioned as Genesis's entry-level luxury sedan, has played a crucial role in establishing the marque's presence in a fiercely competitive segment dominated by German and Japanese competitors. The G90, released in 2017 as Genesis's flagship, helped anchor the brand's ambitions for premium-market credibility.

The timing of this powertrain change carries particular significance: Car and Driver's reporting suggests 2027 could be the G70's final year on sale. If accurate, this would mark a strategic shift for Genesis's model lineup, possibly indicating plans to reposition the brand around SUVs and crossovers or to introduce an entirely new entry-level offering. Such decisions typically reflect broader corporate strategy rather than mere component availability.

The turbo-four replacement, while more efficient and cheaper to produce, will inevitably change the G70's character and appeal. Enthusiasts and luxury buyers accustomed to V-6 refinement and performance may find the consolidated engine option less compelling. Yet from Genesis's perspective, the consolidation aligns with the brand's broader design philosophy and manufacturing realities at its primary production facility in Ulsan, South Korea.

title: Genesis Reveals Details on the Upcoming GV80 Hybrid’s Powertrain
summary: A new four-cylinder hybrid powertrain is coming to the mid-size SUV, and it should arrive in the U.S. sooner rather than later.
whatHappening: Genesis is unveiling powertrain details for a hybrid version of its GV80 mid-size luxury SUV. The new model will feature a four-cylinder hybrid engine and is expected to launch in the U.S. market in the near future.
whoInvolved: Genesis, the luxury division of Hyundai, is behind the development. The GV80 is Genesis's mid-size luxury crossover SUV that has established the brand in the competitive premium SUV segment.
whyMatters: The introduction of a hybrid powertrain expands the GV80's appeal to fuel-conscious luxury buyers while helping Genesis meet tightening emissions standards. An earlier-than-expected U.S. arrival could give Genesis a competitive edge in the growing hybrid luxury SUV market.
articleBody:
Genesis is moving forward with electrification of its popular GV80 lineup, revealing details about a new hybrid powertrain that will reach American consumers ahead of many industry projections. The four-cylinder hybrid engine represents the automaker's latest push to balance performance and efficiency in the luxury crossover segment, according to Car and Driver.

The Genesis GV80, which is a mid-size luxury crossover SUV manufactured and marketed by Genesis, has quickly become a cornerstone product for Hyundai's premium brand since its introduction. The addition of a hybrid variant underscores Genesis's commitment to offering consumers more sustainable powertrain options without compromising the luxury experience that defines the marque.

While full technical specifications remain under wraps, the four-cylinder hybrid configuration signals a strategic departure from traditional gasoline-only engines, positioning the GV80 to compete directly with hybrid offerings from established luxury competitors. The timing of a near-term U.S. market entry suggests Genesis views demand for electrified luxury vehicles as both immediate and significant.

For potential buyers, the hybrid GV80 promises improved fuel economy compared to its conventional counterparts while retaining the premium interior appointments and advanced technology features expected at this price point. Genesis has not yet confirmed an official launch date, but industry observers expect the vehicle to arrive before the end of the year.

The move reflects broader industry momentum toward electrification across all vehicle segments, with luxury automakers increasingly viewing hybrid and electric powertrains as essential to their product portfolios. Genesis's decision to introduce the GV80 hybrid relatively quickly demonstrates the brand's agility in responding to market preferences and regulatory pressures.

title: 2027 Ford F-150 Raptor Gets a Price Cut to Challenge Its Ram Rival
summary: The Raptor costs less for 2027 to better compete with the Ram 1500 RHO, but it also comes with fewer standard features.
whatHappening: Ford is lowering the price of its 2027 F-150 Raptor to undercut the Ram 1500 RHO in the high-performance truck segment. The cost reduction comes with a trade-off: fewer standard features bundled into the base model.
whoInvolved: Ford Motor Company manufactures the F-150 Raptor, part of its F-Series line of full-size pickup trucks that have been in production since 1948. Ram Trucks, owned by Stellantis North America, markets the Ram 1500 RHO as a direct competitor in the premium truck market.
whyMatters: Pricing moves in the performance truck segment signal intensifying competition for affluent truck buyers, a lucrative market segment. This strategy—cutting price while reducing standard equipment—tests whether consumers will accept fewer amenities in exchange for lower sticker prices, potentially reshaping buyer expectations across the premium truck category.
articleBody:
Ford is making an aggressive pricing move with the 2027 F-150 Raptor, cutting its cost to better compete with Ram's 1500 RHO in the premium truck market. According to Car and Driver, the decision to lower the Raptor's price comes with a caveat: the truck now arrives with fewer standard features than before, shifting some equipment that previously came standard into optional packages.

The F-150 Raptor occupies a specific niche within Ford's extensive pickup lineup. The Ford F-Series, which has been manufactured since 1948, includes multiple tiers ranging from the lighter-duty Ranger to the heavy-duty Super Duty series. The Raptor variant targets performance-minded buyers willing to pay premium prices for off-road capability and high-end features. Facing pressure from Ram's 1500 RHO—a relatively newer entrant to the premium truck segment that Stellantis North America began marketing in 2010 as part of Ram's fifth-generation redesign—Ford is adjusting its pricing strategy to remain competitive.

The move reflects a delicate balance Ford must strike in the performance truck market. Reducing the base price makes the Raptor more accessible on paper and helps the nameplate win shopping comparisons against the Ram 1500 RHO. However, by trimming standard features, Ford may push buyers toward higher trim levels or option packages to get the equipment and capabilities they expect, potentially offsetting some of the base-price savings when customers configure their ideal truck.

This pricing approach highlights how competition in the full-size truck segment continues to intensify at the premium end of the market. Both Ford and Ram have invested heavily in performance-oriented variants, recognizing that truck buyers in this segment prioritize capability and features over pure economy. The question now becomes whether Ram will respond with its own pricing adjustments or lean into standard-equipment advantages to differentiate the 1500 RHO.

title: 2028 Genesis GV90
summary: What We Know So Far
whatHappening: Genesis, the luxury brand of South Korea's Hyundai Motor Group, is preparing to launch the 2028 GV90, its flagship three-row SUV. Car and Driver is running down everything known about the vehicle so far.
whoInvolved: Genesis is Hyundai Motor Group's premium automotive brand, designed to compete in the global luxury vehicle market. Hyundai Motor Group itself is a South Korean conglomerate headquartered in Seoul.
whyMatters: The GV90 represents Genesis's continued push into the high-end SUV segment, where demand from affluent buyers remains strong globally. A flagship three-row model signals the brand's ambition to challenge established luxury automakers in the family-vehicle category.
articleBody:
Genesis, the luxury division of South Korea's Hyundai Motor Group, is gearing up to introduce the 2028 GV90, a three-row SUV designed to anchor the brand's lineup at the premium end of the market. According to Car and Driver, details remain limited at this stage, though early information suggests the vehicle will position itself as a direct competitor to established luxury three-row offerings from traditional German and American manufacturers.

The GV90 builds on Genesis's recent expansion into larger SUV formats. articleBody:

The test results validate what the modifications promise: a car that combines the Viper's visceral character with additional grunt that makes it even more aggressive at speed. articleBody:

Its elegant proportions and powerful presence made it a natural candidate for the kind of comprehensive reimagining that Brabus specializes in. However, this project represents a notable shift for Brabus, a company founded in Bottrop in 1977 that has built its reputation primarily on enhancing Mercedes-Benz, Maybach, and Smart vehicles. The decision to tackle an Aston Martin signals the tuner's ambition to reach into the ultra-premium, bespoke supercar space.

It suggests that elite tuners are increasingly willing to pursue one-off or limited-run projects for wealthy clients seeking truly individualized machines, rather than relying solely on volume-oriented customization programs.

The interview with Brabus's CEO likely provides insight into the philosophy and technical challenges behind transforming a mid-2000s grand tourer into a modern hypercar-adjacent machine. title: 1935 Duesenberg SSJ Special Speedster Wins 2026 Pebble Beach Best of Show
summary: A rare supercharged Duesenberg takes the top honor at the 75th annual Concours d'Elegance.
whatHappening: A 1935 Duesenberg SSJ Special Speedster, one of the rarest supercharged automobiles ever built, has claimed the Best of Show award at the 2026 Pebble Beach Concours d'Elegance. The victory marks a significant honor for the historic American luxury marque at the world's most prestigious car show.
whoInvolved: The Duesenberg Automobile & Motors Company, founded in 1920 by brothers Fred and August Duesenberg in Indianapolis, built some of the most celebrated high-performance vehicles of the American automotive golden age. Pebble Beach Concours d'Elegance, held annually at Pebble Beach Golf Links in California, is widely regarded as the pinnacle Concours d'Elegance competition worldwide.
whyMatters: This award underscores the enduring legacy and desirability of American luxury automobiles from the interwar period, cementing the SSJ model's status among collectors and enthusiasts. The recognition reinforces Duesenberg's historical significance as an innovator—the company pioneered the straight-eight engine and four-wheel hydraulic brakes, and was first to win a Grand Prix race with an American car at the 1921 French Grand Prix.
articleBody:
The 1935 Duesenberg SSJ Special Speedster has captured the prestigious Best of Show award at the 75th annual Pebble Beach Concours d'Elegance, cementing its place among the world's most coveted automobiles. The supercharged roadster's victory at this year's competition highlights the enduring appeal of prewar American engineering excellence and design.

Duesenberg Automobile & Motors Company, founded in Indianapolis in 1920 by brothers Fred and August Duesenberg, established itself as a maker of racing and luxury vehicles that would define an era. The company became known for pioneering innovations including the straight-eight engine and four-wheel hydraulic brakes. The marque's competitive pedigree was unmatched in early American motorsport: a Duesenberg was the first American car to win a Grand Prix race, securing victory at the 1921 French Grand Prix, and Duesenberg engines powered Indianapolis 500 winners in 1922, 1924, 1925, and 1927.

The SSJ model represents the pinnacle of Duesenberg's output, with the supercharged variant distinguishing itself as particularly rare and powerful. According to Car and Driver, the specific example that won Best of Show exemplifies the meticulous restoration and preservation standards celebrated at Pebble Beach. The Concours d'Elegance, held annually on the grounds of Pebble Beach Golf Links in California, serves as the finale of Monterey Car Week and is widely considered the most prestigious automotive competition in the world.

The award recognizes not only the vehicle's historical significance but also the exceptional craftsmanship required to bring such an automobile to its present condition. Collectors and enthusiasts view Duesenberg automobiles as irreplaceable artifacts of American industrial achievement during the Golden Age of motoring, a period when domestic manufacturers competed on both engineering sophistication and aesthetic refinement.

This year's Best of Show victory adds to Duesenberg's storied legacy and reinforces the marque's place in automotive history alongside other legendary manufacturers of the era. For collectors, the recognition validates the value and importance of preserving these mechanical and artistic achievements for future generations.

title: Marcus Ericsson Wins Inaugural IndyCar Markham Race with Late Charge Past Romain Grosjean
summary: The Swedish driver earned his extension with Andretti Global, signed earlier this month, with a thrilling drive through the field in the closing laps of the inaugural Markham street race.
whatHappening: Marcus Ericsson has won the inaugural IndyCar race at Markham with a late-race charge that saw him pass Romain Grosjean in the closing laps. The victory comes shortly after Ericsson signed an extension with his team, Andretti Global.
whoInvolved: Marcus Ericsson is a Swedish racing driver competing in the IndyCar Series for Andretti Global, the American motorsports organization fielding teams across multiple racing disciplines. Ericsson previously competed in Formula One from 2014 to 2018 and won the Indianapolis 500 in 2022 with Chip Ganassi Racing.
whyMatters: The win validates Ericsson's contract extension with Andretti Global, signed earlier this month, by delivering a competitive result in a new street race venue. Strong performance in inaugural events can help establish a circuit's reputation and draw future competitors, while Ericsson's victory reinforces his standing as a proven winner in American open-wheel racing.
articleBody:
Marcus Ericsson delivered a commanding performance at the inaugural IndyCar race in Markham, storming through the field in the final laps to overtake Romain Grosjean and claim victory. The Swedish driver's thrilling drive showcased his racecraft and competitive hunger, capping off what has been a productive period for both Ericsson and his team.

The win arrives at a particularly significant moment for Ericsson. Earlier this month, the driver signed an extension to continue with Andretti Global, the American motorsports organization that campaigns teams across the IndyCar Series, Indy NXT, Formula E, and other major racing platforms. By securing a victory in such dramatic fashion—overtaking a former Formula One rival late in the race—Ericsson has immediately justified the team's confidence in his future with the squad.

Ericsson brings considerable pedigree to Andretti. The 33-year-old Swedish driver competed in Formula One from 2014 to 2018, accumulating experience against some of the world's elite drivers. Since transitioning to American open-wheel racing, he has established himself as a frontline competitor. Most notably, Ericsson won the Indianapolis 500 in 2022 while driving for Chip Ganassi Racing, one of IndyCar's most storied organizations. That victory underscored his ability to perform when the stakes are highest, and his Markham triumph adds to a growing résumé of success stateside.

The Markham street race itself represents a new addition to the IndyCar calendar, and Ericsson's victory provides a successful launch for the venue. Inaugural races carry particular importance in establishing a circuit's credibility and appeal to teams, drivers, and fans. According to Road & Track, Ericsson's late-race pass and win demonstrated the kind of competitive racing that can define a new event and generate momentum for future editions.

For Andretti Global, the result underscores the organization's ability to field competitive drivers across its IndyCar operations. As the team continues to expand—the organization's parent company, TWG Motorsports, is set to operate the Cadillac Formula One Team starting in 2026—victories like Ericsson's help build a winning culture and attract sponsor and partner interest. The Markham victory, achieved through driving skill and strategic execution in the closing stages, signals that Ericsson remains a valuable asset to the team's championship ambitions.

title: 2027 Lamborghini Revuelto SV Gains More Power and Downforce
summary: The Super Veloce moniker is back, honing Lamborghini's V-12 hybrid supercar into a track-ready toy with a new fixed rear wing and manually adjustable dampers.
whatHappening: Lamborghini is introducing a track-focused Super Veloce variant of its Revuelto V12 hybrid supercar for 2027. The new SV model adds a fixed rear wing and manually adjustable dampers to boost performance and handling on the circuit.
whoInvolved: Lamborghini, the Italian luxury sports car manufacturer based in Sant'Agata Bolognese and owned by the Volkswagen Group through its Audi subsidiary, is developing the Revuelto SV. The model builds on the standard Revuelto, the brand's flagship V12 hybrid supercar.
whyMatters: The SV designation signals Lamborghini's commitment to creating dedicated high-performance variants that appeal to track enthusiasts and collectors seeking extreme versions of its hypercars. This move reflects the company's strategy of leveraging its V12 hybrid powertrain across multiple market segments, from road-focused to circuit-ready applications.
articleBody:
Lamborghini is reviving its Super Veloce nameplate with a track-tuned version of the Revuelto supercar arriving in 2027. According to Car and Driver, the Revuelto SV adds a fixed rear wing and manually adjustable dampers to the company's flagship V12 hybrid, transforming the grand-touring machine into a circuit-ready weapon with greater power output and aerodynamic downforce.

The Super Veloce badge carries significant historical weight in Lamborghini's lineage, historically applied to the most aggressive, performance-oriented versions of the brand's most celebrated models. By applying it to the Revuelto, the Italian manufacturer signals its intention to push the hybrid supercar beyond its original grand-touring purpose into pure track territory. The fixed rear wing replaces the variable wing system found on the standard Revuelto, trading adjustability for raw aerodynamic efficiency at high speeds.

The manually adjustable damper system represents another shift toward driver engagement and track optimization. Unlike the adaptive systems in the base model, fixed damper settings allow drivers to dial in their preferred suspension tune for specific circuit conditions. Lamborghini has not yet released specific power figures for the SV variant, but the announcement confirms that the new model will produce more horsepower than the standard Revuelto.

Automobili Lamborghini S.p.A., as the company is formally known, has built its reputation on combining dramatic design with cutting-edge engineering. The Revuelto itself marked a watershed moment for the brand, introducing a V12 engine—a twelve-cylinder configuration with two banks of six cylinders arranged in a V around a common crankshaft—alongside hybrid technology for the first time in the company's history.

The SV variant arrives as automakers increasingly segment their high-performance lineups between comfort-focused and track-focused versions. By offering a dedicated Super Veloce model, Lamborghini provides collectors and drivers with a choice tailored to their priorities: the standard Revuelto for everyday supercar duties and long-distance travel, and the SV for those seeking maximum circuit performance and bragging rights among peers.

title: 1995 America Luxorunners: Cadillac vs. Lincoln

whoInvolved: Cadillac Motor Car Division, GM's luxury vehicle brand that has historically dominated the American luxury market, faces off against Lincoln Motor Company, Ford's luxury marque. whyMatters: This comparison captures a critical moment in American automotive luxury, when domestic brands still held significant sway before European marques like BMW and Mercedes began their market dominance in the following decades. The outcome reflects which American luxury vision—GM's or Ford's—resonates most with buyers seeking the finest domestic luxury vehicles of the mid-1990s.
articleBody:
The luxury sedan market in 1995 remains a battleground where Cadillac and Lincoln represent the last great champions of American automotive prestige. Both manufacturers are fielding their finest four-door offerings, each claiming the title of America's most desirable luxury automobile. According to Car and Driver, the comparison centers on fleet, fancy vehicles that embody the aspirations of their respective corporate parents.

Cadillac Motor Car Division, the luxury vehicle division of General Motors, brings decades of heritage to the competition. Historically, Cadillac automobiles have occupied the pinnacle of the luxury field within the United States, with the brand's very name becoming synonymous with American automotive excellence. The division's major markets are the United States, Canada, and China, though Cadillac models are also distributed across 34 additional markets worldwide. For the 1995 model year, Cadillac's entry represents the latest expression of this venerable tradition.

Lincoln Motor Company, Ford's luxury brand, offers its own interpretation of what American luxury should embody. The two manufacturers have competed in this space for generations, each cultivating a distinct identity and customer base. The 1995 comparison allows both brands to showcase their understanding of comfort, engineering, and the intangible qualities that define luxury in the American market.

What makes this moment significant is that 1995 represents a high-water mark for domestic luxury dominance. Cadillac has historically competed with Lincoln for supremacy among American buyers seeking the finest vehicles money can buy. Yet the competitive landscape would shift dramatically in the decades to come, as European luxury brands would eventually outsell Cadillac and similar American marques. For now, however, both Cadillac and Lincoln remain formidable competitors in the segment they essentially created.

The four-door sedan format itself reflects the priorities of 1995 luxury buyers: practicality combined with opulence, family-friendly dimensions wrapped in premium materials and power. Both vehicles offer the kind of space, smoothness, and appointments that defined American luxury for generations. The comparison between them offers buyers a clear choice between two distinctly American visions of what the luxury sedan should be.
